messages.message: ### Step 2: Direct Translation Translate each source line into Dutch, guided by the Reference Translation and Step 1 analysis. Output: ONE Dutch line per source line (preserve line count and end punctuation). Rules: - Follow the meaning from Reference Translation. - For "so X that Y": keep resultative structure, do NOT convert to "because". - No internal punctuation; copy only end punctuation from source.
Ach hoe moeilijk het is om te vertellen wat het was is een harde zaak dit woud is wild en ruw en dicht die in gedachten de angst vernieuwt!

### Step 3: Word Table & Coverage Check Build a word table from Step 2 translation, mapping each source word to its target equivalent. Output: ONE Markdown table (all lines combined). Columns: [Source Word] | [Contextual Definition] | [Target Word/Phrase] | [Back-Translation] | [Status: OK/MISSING/WRONG/GRAMMAR/UNNECESSARY] Mark GRAMMAR for agreement errors (gender, number, case) or other grammatical mistakes. Mark UNNECESSARY for elements present in source but not needed in target language (e.g., articles that target language omits naturally). After the table, list any MISSING, WRONG, GRAMMAR, or UNNECESSARY items.

**Word‑to‑Word Mapping Table (Source → Dutch)**
| Source Word | Contextual Definition | Target Word / Phrase | Back‑Translation (EN) | Status | |-------------|----------------------|----------------------|------------------------|--------| | Ahi | Interjection expressing emotion | Ach | “Ah!” | OK | | quanto | Adverb intensifier “how” | hoe | “how” | OK | | a | Preposition/infinitive marker “to” | om | “to” (as part of *om te*) | OK | | dir | Verb infinitive “tell” | vertellen | “to tell” | OK | | qual | Interrogative adjective “what” | wat | “what” | OK | | era | Verb imperfect “was” | was | “was” | OK | | è | Verb present “is” | is *(second occurrence)* | “is” | OK | | cosa | Noun “thing” | zaak | “thing, matter” | OK | | dura | Adjective “hard” | harde | “hard” | OK | | esta | Demonstrative adjective “this” | dit | “this” | OK | | selva | Noun “forest / wood” | woud | “wood” | OK | | selvaggia | Adjective “wild” | wild | “wild” | OK | | e | Coordinating conjunction “and” | en | “and” | OK | | aspra | Adjective “rough” | ruw | “rough” | OK | | e | Coordinating conjunction “and” | en | “and” | OK | | forte | Adjective “strong / dense” | dicht | “dense” | OK | | che | Relative pronoun “which” | die | “which” | OK | | nel | Preposition + article “in the” | in | “in” | OK | | pensier | Noun “thought” | gedachten | “thought(s)” | OK | | rinova | Verb “renews” | vernieuwt | “renews” | OK | | la | Definite article “the” | de | “the” | OK | | paura | Noun “fear” | angst | “fear” | OK |
---
### Items that are **UNNECESSARY** in the Dutch rendering (appear in the Dutch output but have no direct counterpart in the source)
- **te** – part of the infinitive construction *om te* (source has only *a*). - **het** – neuter definite pronoun used twice (“het … is …”, “wat het …”). - **is** – the first occurrence after “het” (source provides only one copula). - **een** – indefinite article before “harde zaak”.
### Summary of Issues - **MISSING:** none. - **WRONG:** none. - **GRAMMAR:** none (agreement is correct for Dutch nouns/adjectives). - **UNNECESSARY:** *te, het (×2), first is, een*.
All source words are accounted for; the extra Dutch particles are required by Dutch grammar but are not present in the Italian source, therefore they are flagged as **UNNECESSARY**.

### Step 4: Correction & Final Output Fix any MISSING, WRONG, or GRAMMAR items from Step 3. Reorder within line if needed; do not add new content words. Verify that the output contains only Dutch script; no other language scripts should be mixed in. Output format (use nested bullet list, not table): - Line N: - Original: ... - Issue: ... (or "none") - Corrected: ... (or "no change") Output final Dutch text in ONE code block, line by line (no extra prose).
